## Video 1 — `layer_print_visibility`

### What is visible

- **Website surface:** The D&D Beyond navigation, loading splash, cookie/privacy dialog, character artwork, statistics, actions, and ordinary character-sheet layout are D&D Beyond’s own product.
- **Extension work:** By approximately 31 seconds, the extension adds:
  - A dark, gold-accented control panel on the left with sections such as **LAYOUT** and **OUTPUT**.
  - A dark **LAYER MANAGEMENT** panel on the right.
  - A **SHAPES** group in that panel with the three-state control labeled **Print only**, **Both**, and **Screen only**.
  - A first-run hint card explaining how to drag sections, with a **Got it** button.
  - A dark notice stating **“No saved layout yet — the default template is loaded.”**
  - Gold/red outlines around enhanced sheet sections, making the extension’s modifications distinguishable from the base website.
- Around 30 seconds, the recording switches to a print-oriented rendering:
  - The extension’s floating control panel and Layer Management panel are absent.
  - A largely white print page remains, with some enhanced sheet sections visible at the top and left.
- No extension-owned “loading…” or other activation-transition overlay is shown. The loading spinner belongs to the **D&D Beyond website**, not the extension.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Assertion | On-camera status | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Layer Management panel is hidden inside `@media print` | **VISIBLE** | The print rendering does not show the extension’s Layer Management panel or other floating extension controls. |
| Locked layers are forced fully opaque on print | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No clearly locked layer and its before/after print opacity are visibly identified. |
| “Disable on Print” marks the layer container and hides it in print CSS | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No Disable on Print operation or resulting marked container is shown. |
| Re-enabling clears `data-print-disabled` and its hide rule | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No re-enabling operation is shown, and DOM attributes/rules cannot be verified visually. |
| Every layer group carries the three-state strip, naming all three modes | **NOT-VISIBLE** | One **SHAPES** group visibly offers **Print only / Both / Screen only**, but the video does not establish that every layer group has the strip. |
| **Print only** hides the layer on screen and undoes that hide at print time | **NOT-VISIBLE** | The mode is visible, but no associated screen-hide and print-reveal comparison is shown. |
| **Screen only** stays visible now and is skipped on print | **NOT-VISIBLE** | The mode is visible, but no associated screen/print behavior is demonstrated. |
| **Both** clears both flags and both print rules | **NOT-VISIBLE** | The option is visible, but selecting it and clearing the resulting behavior are not shown. |

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

**Working affordances observed:**

- The extension UI is clearly distinguishable from D&D Beyond through its dark codex/workbench styling, gold hairlines, and custom typography.
- The Layer Management panel provides organized **SECTIONS** and **SHAPES** groups.
- The three print modes are labeled in a compact, understandable strip.
- The first-run hint is clearly styled and includes an actionable **Got it** control.
- The “No saved layout yet” notice communicates the default-template state.
- The print rendering successfully omits the extension’s screen-only management UI.

**Missing or rough affordances:**

- **No extension-owned activation/loading transition is visible.** The enhancement and panels appear without a brief “Enhancing…” or equivalent state. The D&D Beyond spinner is website behavior and cannot count as extension feedback.
- No error state is demonstrated.
- Disabled controls are visible—particularly the muted left-panel controls—but the video does not show whether attempting to use them explains why they are disabled.
- The three-state control is shown only for Shapes; its consistency across every layer group is not demonstrated.
- The print behavior is only weakly illustrated: the panel disappears, but individual layer-mode outcomes are not shown clearly enough to verify the contract.

**Video verdict: PARTIAL.** The print-hidden manager is visibly demonstrated, but most asserted print-mode behaviors are absent or not visually verifiable.

---

## Video 2 — `layer_reorder_keyboard`

### What is visible

- **Website surface:** The D&D Beyond loading splash, navigation bar, character artwork, character name, abilities, actions, and base sheet content are the website’s own surfaces.
- **Extension work:**
  - The same dark left control panel and right Layer Management panel appear.
  - The sheet is enhanced with outlined and repositioned section containers.
  - A centered dark toast appears reading **“Layer order updated.”**
  - The toast is accompanied by a small gold square/icon and later fades away.
  - The top row of sheet sections changes horizontal order around the same time as the toast.
- The keyboard presses themselves, focused row, highlighted rows, locked-row state, and mouse drag interaction are not visibly identifiable on camera.

### Layer 1 — Asserted-behavior evidence

| Assertion | On-camera status | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| ArrowUp moves the tail layer exactly one slot toward the head through the row’s keydown handler | **NOT-VISIBLE** | A reorder and “Layer order updated” toast are visible, but the pressed key, focused row, and exact one-slot ArrowUp operation are not shown. |
| ArrowDown moves a layer one slot toward the tail, with mirror-image stacks | **NOT-VISIBLE** | The ArrowDown operation and resulting mirror-image stack are not visibly demonstrated. |
| Three rapid presses—Up, Down, Up—leave all actions on the same layer without manual re-clicking (`restoreRowFocus`) | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No rapid sequence or retained focus is shown. A single toast cannot establish the required sequence or focus restoration. |
| Home moves a layer to the head in one press | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No Home-key operation is shown. |
| End moves a layer to the tail in one press | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No End-key operation is shown. |
| A locked row’s arrows are a no-op, with no stack change and no undo entry | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No clearly locked row is operated with an arrow key, and undo history is not shown. |
| Already-at-boundary arrow presses are safe no-ops with depth untouched | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No boundary operation or depth measurement is shown. |
| Keyboard writes a stack positionally identical to a drag/drop write for the same swap | **NOT-VISIBLE** | No mouse drag/drop comparison is shown. |

### Layer 2 — Product-aim conformance

**Working affordances observed:**

- The extension is visually unmistakable against the D&D Beyond page: dark floating panels, gold dividers, gold accents, and outlined sheet boxes.
- The **“Layer order updated”** toast gives clear feedback after a reorder and disappears after a short interval.
- The layer groups and section lists are organized into a dedicated management panel rather than mixing controls into the website.
- The enhanced sheet’s moved/outlined sections provide visual feedback in the page itself.
- A first-run hint card and “Got it” action are available.
- Muted controls visibly indicate disabled states in the left panel.

**Missing or rough affordances:**

- **No extension-owned activation/loading transition is visible.** The panels and enhanced layout pop in without a dedicated “Enhancing…” or “Loading…” state.
- The reorder feedback is present, but there is no visible focus indicator or keyboard-help affordance explaining ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Home, and End.
- The “Layer order updated” toast does not identify which layer moved or where it moved, so the feedback is less informative than the behavior being tested.
- No keyboard focus restoration is visibly demonstrated.
- Locked-row feedback, boundary no-op feedback, and undo behavior are not demonstrated.
- No error state is shown.
- The toolbar ON badge is not visible in the sampled frames, so the extension’s active/inactive state cannot be reviewed here.

**Video verdict: PARTIAL.** The camera shows a real extension-driven reorder and a working toast, but it does not witness the specified keyboard behaviors or their required edge cases.

## Overall certification result

The extension UI is strongly distinguishable from the website, and the Layer Management panel, first-run hint, disabled states, print-panel hiding, and reorder toast are visible. However, the videos do not visibly demonstrate most of the precise print-mode and keyboard-reorder assertions. Both also lack a dedicated extension-owned activation/loading transition.

VERDICT: PARTIAL
